bib.title: Lakehouse: A New Generation of Open Platforms that Unify Data Warehousing and Advanced Analytics
bib.venue: CIDR '21 (11th Annual Conference on Innovative Data Systems Research), January 11-15, 2021, Online

question: Can data lakes on open formats such as Parquet and ORC become high-performance systems offering warehouse management features plus direct I/O for ML, replacing the two-tier lake plus warehouse architecture?
hypothesis: The data warehouse architecture will wane and be replaced by the Lakehouse: open direct-access formats, first-class ML/data-science support, and state-of-the-art performance.
contributions: Argues the case for the Lakehouse against the first-generation warehouse and second-generation two-tier architectures
Sketches a design: transactional metadata layer over object store, format-independent SQL optimizations (caching, auxiliary data, data layout), declarative DataFrame access for ML
Reports TPC-DS results for Databricks Delta Engine vs four cloud data warehouses

results.claim: The two-tier lake plus warehouse architecture is dominant, used at virtually all Fortune 500 enterprises, in the authors' experience.
The Lakehouse is defined as low-cost directly accessible storage plus ACID transactions, versioning, auditing, indexing, caching and query optimization.

limits: Benchmark is a single TPC-DS run by the vendor (Databricks) comparing against anonymised warehouses DW1-DW4; no repetitions, configuration, or tuning details are given.
Authors concede Delta Lake, Iceberg and Hudi support transactions on one table at a time only; cross-table transactions are future work.
Transaction log on object store limits transactions per second because of object store latency.
Direct access gives up data independence: the storage format becomes part of the system's public API.
Hudi does not support concurrent writers (as of 2021).
Paper is a prediction (2021); the claim that warehouses will wither is not tested. Warehouses have since added open table format support, which post-dates the paper.
Only authors' experience supports claims of Fortune 500 prevalence and Delta Lake adoption.

terms.definition: a data management system based on low-cost and directly-accessible storage that also provides traditional analytical DBMS management and performance features such as ACID transactions, data versioning, auditing, indexing, caching, and query optimization
collecting data from operational databases into centralized warehouses with schema-on-write for decision support and BI
offloading all raw data into data lakes (low-cost storage with a file API, open formats), schema-on-read, with a small subset ETLed to a downstream warehouse
low-cost storage systems with a file API that hold data in generic and usually open file formats, such as Apache Parquet and ORC

a transactional layer over object store storage that defines which objects are part of a table version, implementing ACID transactions, versioning, schema enforcement, constraints, access control and audit logging
